node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Missing value symbols
node.description: Use symbols or letters to represent unknown values in number sentences and simple situations.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Variable notation
node.description: Read and write letters as variables that can stand for unknown or varying values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Variables in contexts
node.description: Define variables to represent quantities in worded and contextual situations.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Expressions versus equations
node.description: Distinguish algebraic expressions from equations and understand what each represents.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Substitute positive values
node.description: Evaluate expressions by replacing variables with positive whole-number or decimal values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Substitute negative values
node.description: Evaluate expressions by replacing variables with negative values while preserving expression structure.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Evaluate algebraic expressions
node.description: Evaluate algebraic expressions using substitution and conventional order of operations.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Substitute into formulas
node.description: Use formulas by substituting known values and evaluating the resulting expression.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Terms coefficients and constants
node.description: Identify terms, coefficients, variables and constants in algebraic expressions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Algebraic conventions
node.description: Use algebraic notation conventions such as omitted multiplication signs and standard term order.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Like and unlike terms
node.description: Identify terms with the same variable part as like terms and distinguish unlike terms.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Collect like terms
node.description: Simplify expressions by combining coefficients of like terms while preserving value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Distributive property in algebra
node.description: Use the distributive property to connect products and sums in algebraic expressions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Expand single brackets
node.description: Expand algebraic expressions with a single bracket using the distributive property.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Factor out common factor
node.description: Factorise expressions by identifying and extracting a common factor from all terms.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Expand and simplify
node.description: Expand brackets and collect like terms to write equivalent simplified expressions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Variable represents a value
node.description: A variable represents a value or quantity, not the name of an object.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Expression has no equality claim
node.description: An expression names a quantity but does not state that two quantities are equal.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Substitution replaces variable
node.description: Substitution replaces each occurrence of a variable with a specified value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Negative substitution needs grouping
node.description: When substituting negative values, grouping symbols can preserve the intended expression structure.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Coefficient multiplies variable
node.description: A coefficient multiplies the variable part of a term.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Like terms have same variable part
node.description: Like terms have the same variable part with the same powers, even if their coefficients differ.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Collecting like terms preserves value
node.description: Combining like terms rewrites an expression in an equivalent form with the same value for all allowed variable values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Algebraic conventions reduce symbols
node.description: Algebraic conventions often omit multiplication signs and write terms in standard forms to reduce clutter.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Distributive property expands brackets
node.description: The factor outside a bracket multiplies every term inside the bracket when expanding.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Factorising reverses expansion
node.description: Factorising rewrites a sum or difference as a product, reversing an expansion step.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Variable is object label
node.description: Learner treats a variable as a label for an object rather than as a number or quantity value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Expression must have equals sign
node.description: Learner thinks an algebraic expression is incomplete unless it includes an equals sign and an answer.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Substitute only first occurrence
node.description: Learner replaces only one occurrence of a variable instead of every occurrence in the expression.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Combine unlike terms
node.description: Learner combines unlike terms as if their variable parts were the same.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Distribute to first term only
node.description: Learner multiplies only the first term inside brackets when expanding an expression.

edge.rationale: Missing-value symbols are an early bridge into variables as unknown values.
Variable notation is central to interpreting letters as values.
Defining variables in contexts practises interpreting variables as quantities.
Distinguishing expressions and equations supports accurate variable interpretation.
Substituting positive values is an early core form of substitution.
Substituting negative values extends substitution to signed-number expressions.
Evaluating expressions directly practises substitution and operation order.
Using formulas is a common application of substitution into structured expressions.
Terms, coefficients and constants are foundational for simplifying expressions.
Algebraic conventions support reading and simplifying expressions accurately.
Identifying like terms is essential for collecting them.
Collecting like terms is a core simplifying-expression procedure.
The distributive property is the structure behind expansion and factorisation.
Expanding single brackets directly practises expansion using distribution.
Factoring out a common factor is an early core form of factorising.
Expanding and simplifying combines distribution with collecting like terms.
Missing-value symbols build on number sentences and relational equality.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats a box or letter as an operation rather than a value placeholder.

edge.rationale: Letter variables extend earlier missing-value symbols and placeholders.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads a variable only as a label rather than as a value that can be reasoned about.

edge.rationale: Defining variables in context requires first understanding variable notation as representing a quantity.
edge.failure_signal: Learner chooses letters based on object names but cannot state the quantity represented.

edge.rationale: Distinguishing expressions and equations requires recognising variables inside algebraic statements and expressions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner adds an equals sign and answer to every expression regardless of task.

edge.rationale: Substitution requires understanding that a variable can be replaced by a given value.
edge.failure_signal: Learner leaves the variable unchanged or substitutes inconsistently.

edge.rationale: Substituting negative values requires preserving signs and operation order in integer expressions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner loses the negative sign or changes expression structure during substitution.

edge.rationale: Evaluating algebraic expressions requires substituting values before calculating.
edge.failure_signal: Learner performs operations on variables before replacing them with values.

edge.rationale: Using formulas requires evaluating structured algebraic expressions after substitution.
edge.failure_signal: Learner substitutes values but does not follow formula structure or operation order.

edge.rationale: Identifying terms and constants requires reading an algebraic expression as a structured quantity.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify where one term ends and another begins.

edge.rationale: Algebraic conventions are meaningful after terms, coefficients and variables are understood.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads 3x as a two-digit number or as 3 plus x.

edge.rationale: Like-term identification depends on understanding term structure and variable parts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner groups terms by coefficient alone or variable letter alone when powers differ.

edge.rationale: Collecting like terms requires identifying which terms are like before combining coefficients.
edge.failure_signal: Learner combines unlike terms or changes the variable part during simplification.

edge.rationale: Algebraic distribution extends the distributive property from whole-number multiplication to terms with variables.
edge.failure_signal: Learner distributes mechanically without recognising multiplication over addition.

edge.rationale: Expanding single brackets is a direct application of the distributive property.
edge.failure_signal: Learner multiplies only the first term inside brackets or drops signs.

edge.rationale: Factoring out a common factor reverses the distributive structure used in expansion.
edge.failure_signal: Learner identifies a common number but cannot rewrite the expression as a product.

edge.rationale: Expanding and simplifying requires first being able to expand brackets correctly.
edge.failure_signal: Learner expands but leaves unlike or like terms incorrectly combined.
